title: ‘You Know What I Like’—Thierry Henry Can’t Get Enough of USMNT’s Next Superstar
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom11:00 AM EDTThierry Henry was impressed by the USMNT’s recent window. / Ercin Erturk/Anadolu/Getty ImagesThierry Henry was full of praise for U.S. men’s national team’s young gem Cavan Sullivan, singling out the same quality which so enamored the teenager to Mauricio Pochettino.

Sullivan had an international break to savor. The Philadelphia Union forward made his senior debut, turned 17 and became the youngest scorer in the history of the program this fall. Pochettino doesn’t tend to single out individuals but made an exception to hail the grit, rather than the glitz, Sullivan had demonstrated. Henry was similarly impressed.

“You know what I like, is his demeanor, his attitude,” Henry gushed on CBS Golazo this week. “Swagger,” was another trait offered up by presenter Kate Abdo which the former Arsenal and Barcelona forward accepted.
“He plays, he goes about it, he will put his foot in,” Henry added. “He also has an eye for a pass or for a goal. But he will not back down for anyone, although he’s young.”

Sullivan’s star is on the rise. Each game seems to bring a new record for the royally in-form teen, who has directly contributed to at least one goal in each of his previous seven club appearances. Yet, Henry’s expectations haven’t been sated: “I think he can do even more.”

Henry also shifted the spotlight toward the manager who called up Sullivan and a hoard of other youngsters. “You have to a lot of credit to Pochettino: He allowed those guys to come,” the retired France international pointed out.

Sullivan was one of eight teenagers handed his debut during fall’s four friendlies, with six of that contingent plying their trade in Major League Soccer. Unlike some previous USMNT managers who have prioritized players with minimal European experience above any domestic action, Pochettino has wholeheartedly embraced home-based talent.
“It will be good for the MLS, because I think some of the guys coming from the MLS were not looked at so much, some times before,” Henry pointed out. “And now that’s not the case.

“Sometimes, I feel that I believe more—more, more, much more—in the talent of the players here in the USA than people that talk in the [U.S.] media,” Pochettino claimed earlier this month. “Because I think it’s so important to translate that you really trust. And then because we [have] expertise, that is why we are here, don’t worry that we are going to make the best decision.
“It’s so important that the people really trust in the process, trust in our decisions, but trust in the players and respect the players.”

Pochettino has an admirer in Henry, although his faith isn’t concrete just yet. “It looks like it can be a bright future,” the Premier League icon concluded, “but it remains to be seen if it can carry on.”
